today r1: critic picked Things on desktop, Things on phone — gap: desktop: The loser ends the This Evening list with an extra, focused 'New To-Do' row: a dashed 24px placeholder checkbox and a 4px-wide, ~36px-tall #659DE9 caret at x~119 that nearly touches the placeholder text (about 1px gap) and runs about 10px taller than the 26px title line. It is heavy and not native, and it pulls the eye away from the real rows. The winner ends cleanly after 'Buy party decorations'. Fix: do not auto-open an editing row in the resting Today state, and if one is shown, use a 2px caret the height of the text line with about 2px of clearance.  ·  phone: The loser's checkboxes are drawn half a pixel off the grid. The left and top strokes blur into a pale 2px (~#D2D2D2), while the right and bottom are a crisp, darker 1px (~#BDBDBD), so all eight boxes look lopsided and bleed to 23px wide. The winner draws an even ~1.5px #BFC1C4 stroke on all four sides of a 21x21 box. Fix: snap the checkbox rect to whole or half pixels so every side renders the same weight. A secondary fix is to darken the subtitles from ~#A1A5AA to ~#96989B to match the winner's contrast.

quickfind r1: pair ready for the critic — Rebuilt Quick Find to Things' measured geometry: 297pt panel with hairline frame, 26pt field, Things magnifier/X, thick blue caret, 22pt rows on 23pt pitch, 14pt pies, badge/count/check sizing, olive active star; phone field/Cancel/hint aligned

quickfind r1: critic picked ours on desktop, Things on phone — gap: phone: The loser's empty-state greys are washed out. The hint 'Quickly switch lists, find to-dos...' is at about #A8A8AA on #F9F9FB (~2.3:1), the 'Quick Find' placeholder at about #8F949A, and 'Cancel' at about #4F5051. The winner uses about #A0A0A1 for the hint (~2.6:1), #86888A for the placeholder and #434445 for Cancel, which gives firmer, more legible type at the same sizes.

detail r1: critic picked Things on desktop, ours on phone — gap: desktop: The 'May 25' date chip in the list below the card is badly set. In the loser, the chip text sits high in its 26px pill (4px above the digits, 8px below), so its baseline is about 4px above the baseline of 'Print handouts for attendees' next to it. The winner centres the text in the pill (6px above, 6px below) and keeps its baseline within 1px of the row title. Fix it by vertically centring the chip label on cap height and aligning the chip's text baseline to the row title's baseline.

today r2: critic picked Things on desktop, Things on phone — gap: desktop: The deadline label on the 'Finish expense report' row (right edge, ~17px pink #FF2D55-ish 'today') is set in regular weight with ~1.5px strokes, so it looks spindly and detached beside the solid-filled ~20px flag glyph; the winner sets 'today' in medium (~500) weight at the same size and colour so the flag and label read as one badge with matched stroke weight. Rows, checkboxes (24px, #C0C3C6 stroke), subtitles and the This Evening heading are otherwise pixel-for-pixel equivalent.  ·  phone: The 'today' deadline label at the right of the 'Finish expense report' row (x~430, ~15px) is regular weight and carries ~9% less ink than the winner's, so it looks thin against the solid flag at x~408; the winner uses medium (~500) weight so flag and label balance. The loser's titles are also a hair lighter/smaller (22px vs 23px ascender-to-descender), compounding the slightly washed-out read.
today: deadline 'today' label to medium weight matched to flag; phone title weight/size

detail r2: pair ready for the critic — Date chip: 16px pill with its label centred on cap height and baseline-aligned to the row title (darker label, tighter gap); card title tracking matched; phone double-tap no longer selects a title word; phone checkbox on whole device pixels

detail r2: critic picked Things on desktop, ours on phone — gap: desktop: The loser's lifted card stretches to about 920px, so the notes run at a ~770px measure (~95 characters). The paragraph breaks into one long line plus an orphaned two-word 'version soon.', and the checklist hairlines run ~840px, leaving the when/tags/deadline icons marooned far from the content. The winner's card is ~716px wide, so the notes wrap into two balanced ~585px lines. Fix: cap the card's text measure at ~600-650px (~70 characters).
detail: cap detail card text measure (~640px) so notes wrap balanced and icons sit near content

today r3: pair ready for the critic — Deadline label now medium weight at Things' size (12px desktop / 14px -0.15 tracking phone) with flag aligned; iOS flag redrawn wider with a crisp pole; phone titles 17.8px to match Things' glyph size and ink

detail r3: pair ready for the critic — Desktop card width capped at 31em (Things' 434pt card), so notes and checklist keep Things' ~632px measure and the icons sit under the content; notes get a 5px trailing inset so the paragraph wraps into two balanced lines like Things; notes refit on window resize

detail r3: critic picked Things on desktop, Things on phone — gap: desktop: The lifted card doesn't match the list column. Its left edge overhangs the header rule by about 19px, but its right edge stops about 183px short of where the rule and the ... menu end (card ends at x~760, rule runs to x~943). So the card looks narrower than the list it belongs to and sits lopsided under the header. The winner's card overhangs the column by about 20px on both sides, so it lines up with the header rule and the ... menu.  ·  phone: The completion checkbox next to the title is a thin ~1px hairline in a pale grey (#BBBBBE, 23x23px). Beside the large ~22pt title it fades out, and the most important control on the card reads as disabled. The winner draws the same box with a firmer ~1.5-2px stroke and a slight inner shade, and its when/tag/flag icons are a bit heavier too, so the controls hold their own against the text.

when r2: panel of 3 — desktop 3/3 for ours, phone 0/3 for ours → Things holds — gap: phone: The loser's sheet stops at Someday. It has no 'Add Reminder' row, so there is no way to attach a time from the When sheet, and it closes with only ~27px of padding under Someday. The winner adds a muted secondary row below Someday: a thin ~23px plus at x≈29 and the label in ~#9296A1 grey, on the same ~59px pitch as Today, This Evening and Someday, then ~36px of bottom padding. That finishes the list with a clear quieter tier.  /  The loser ends the sheet at Someday with no '+ Add Reminder' row. The sheet lacks the reminder affordance, and the Someday row sits only ~26px above the bottom edge, so the sheet stops abruptly. The winner adds a quiet grey (about rgb(135,139,150)) '+ Add Reminder' row ~59px below Someday. Its plus glyph sits in the 25-52px icon column, its label lines up with the ~67px text column, and it leaves a ~32px bottom inset.  /  The loser's sheet ends right after the Someday row: the bottom edge is ~25px below the Someday text and there is no Add Reminder footer, so there is no way to set a time and the sheet feels cut short. The winner adds a '+ Add Reminder' row one ~60px pitch below Someday. The plus sits in the icon column at x~40 and the ~#989CA7 grey label lines up with the other labels at x~67, with ~32px of padding before the sheet edge. Add that footer row at the same pitch and alignment.
when: Add a muted '+ Add Reminder' footer row to the phone When sheet on the same pitch, with proper bottom inset

composer r2: panel of 3 — desktop 1/3 for ours, phone 3/3 for ours → Things holds — gap: desktop: The open composer barely separates from the page. The loser sets a #FFFFFF card on a near-white #FAFAFA backdrop, about 2% luminance apart, so the lift depends on a faint shadow whose edge is about #E0E0E0. Its caret is also tall at about 37px, rising about 12px above the cap height. The winner puts the same card on a cool #F2F3F7 grey with a firmer shadow edge of about #D4D4D8, so the editor clearly reads as a raised sheet. Its caret is about 33px. Fix: darken the backdrop to about #F2F2F5 and trim the caret to the font's ascender-to-descender height.  /  The loser sets the white composer card on a near-white #FAFAFA page, only about 5 levels darker than the card, so the card's top and side edges almost disappear and the card is held up only by its bottom shadow. The winner uses a cool #F2F3F7 page, about 12 levels below white, so the same soft shadow outlines the whole card as a clearly raised sheet.
composer: Darken composer backdrop to cool grey so the white card reads as a raised sheet; trim caret height

composer r3: pair ready for the critic — Desktop: while composing, the content pane and toolbar recede to cool grey #f2f3f7 so the white card reads as a raised sheet on all edges (toolbar hover shades adjusted); caret centred on the text line to sit exactly where Things' does

composer r3: panel of 3 — desktop 1/3 for ours, phone 2/3 for ours → Things holds — gap: desktop: Type, checkbox, icons, padding and shadow are pixel-identical, so the difference is the layout: the loser's composer card stretches to ~1110 px wide, which leaves the 4-icon action cluster (calendar/tag/checklist/flag, ~28 px icons at 64 px pitch) about 630 px right of the end of the 20 px title. The row reads as two disconnected islands. The winner caps the card at ~835 px, so the icons sit ~350 px from the title and the card reads as one compact unit. Cap the composer's max-width at ~840 px.  /  Checklist glyph (3rd toolbar icon, ~24x29px, bottom-right of card): the loser draws ~5px bullets with the bottom one squashed almost square, and short hairline dashes that land at ~#C8-#D0, visibly fainter than its own bullets and the neighbouring icons. The winner uses round, even ~6-7px bullets and crisp 1px dashes in the same ~#A8 grey as the rest of the set.
composer: Cap composer width ~840px on desktop; redraw checklist glyph with round even bullets and #A8 dashes

when r3: panel of 3 — desktop 1/3 for ours, phone 0/3 for ours → Things holds — gap: desktop: Row contents sit low in the loser. The pink calendar glyphs hang about 2-3px below their labels: the icon top is flush with the cap line and its bottom falls about 6px under the baseline. The 'in 3 days' label also sits low in the 35px blue selection pill, with about 12px above the caps and about 7px below the baseline. The winner centres both: its about 23px icons overhang the text evenly (about 4px above, about 3px below), and its label has about 10/9px inside the pill. It also uses the same 11px gap between the field and the list as its side margins, where the loser uses 9px. Fix: nudge the icons up about 2px and centre the label in the highlight.  /  The selected 'in 3 days' label sits low inside its blue pill. The loser's highlight spans about y61-97 with the cap top at 74 and the baseline at 89, which leaves about 12px above the text and 7px below. Its first-row text also breaks the 38px row rhythm by 1px. The winner's pill spans about y63-99 around the same 16px cap block, leaving 9.5px above and below, and its 10px gap below the search field matches the 38px row pitch. Move the loser's pill down 2px, or centre it on the row's line box. Also stop fading the calendar icon to a washed-out lavender on the selected row: keep the pink header bar solid, as the winner does.  ·  phone: The 'This Evening' moon hangs low in the loser. Its 28px glyph ends about 6px below the text baseline but starts only about 3px above the cap line, so it looks dropped against the label. The winner centres the moon on the cap height (about 4px over, about 3px under), matching how the star sits next to 'Today'. The loser's calendar rows are also spaced unevenly (61/63/61px), where the winner keeps a steady 62px rhythm. Fix: raise the moon about 2-3px and snap the grid rows to one pitch.  /  The 'This Evening' moon hangs about 3px low. In the loser it spans about y166-193 against a cap block of y168-186, with 2px above the cap top and 7px below the baseline, so it sags under the text. The winner's moon spans y163-190, with about 5px above and 4px below, centred on the cap height like the star next to 'Today'. The loser's calendar grid also steps 61/63/61px between rows where the winner holds an even 62/62/62, and the stacked 'Jun 1' sits 1.5px low in its row. Nudge the moon up 3px and snap the grid rows to one integer pitch.  /  The This Evening moon glyph (~24x25px) sits about 3px low: its centre is at y~180 against the text's cap-height midline at ~177, so its bottom hangs below the baseline. The winner centres a ~22x25px moon on the midline, the same way the star centres on Today. Nudge it up 3px or centre it on cap height.
when: Center desktop icons and selected label in pill, raise phone moon, even 62px phone grid rows

composer r4: pair ready for the critic — Desktop composer card capped at 418px (Things' card width) so the action icons sit with the title; checklist glyph redrawn on the pixel grid with round even bullets and crisp 1px rules (plus an iOS-proportioned variant on phone); phone checkbox ring thickened to 1.5px

composer r4: panel of 3 — desktop 1/3 for ours, phone 3/3 for ours → Things holds — gap: desktop: Card elevation: the loser's shadow is short and hard, a dark rim (~#C4C2C8) about 3px under the card that is mostly gone within ~20px (~#E6E7EB at 15px below), so the open to-do looks pasted onto the #F2F3F7 background. The winner uses a softer, deeper drop (peak ~#C6C6C6, easing over ~35px, still ~#E1E1E1 at 15px below) that reads as a lifted editing card. Soften the loser's shadow to about y 4px / blur 24-30px / ~12% black.  /  In the bottom-right toolbar (icons at ~x610-830, y230-258) the loser's calendar glyph has a heavy double-stroke header band (top edge plus a full-width divider ~2px below) and its checklist bullets run straight into their dashes with ~1px air, so the cluster reads dark and cramped; the winner draws a single thin inset header rule and leaves ~2-3px between each 6px bullet and its dash.

Phone: moon refit to Things' crescent and centred on cap height, star nudged up, grid on an integer 46px pitch (no 61/63 wobble), Jun 1 centred, labels 1px left, sheet edge ring

today r5: panel of 3 — desktop 0/3 for ours, phone 3/3 for ours → Things holds — gap: desktop: The loser's This Evening heading block is a hair weaker: the moon is a chunkier crescent (~28x29px, fat body, blunt tips, ~4% more ink) that reads as a blob beside the bold label, and the label itself sets ~1.7% narrower and lighter (172px vs 175px wide). The winner uses a slimmer crescent with finer tips and a marginally heavier, more assertive heading, so the section break reads cleaner. Everything else (24px checkbox, 20px checkbox-to-title gap, 76px row pitch, #808082 subtitles, flag/today pill) is pixel-identical.  /  Rows are otherwise pixel-identical (24px checkbox, 20px checkbox-to-title gap, 76px row pitch, same greys), but the loser lets the list column run about 1066px wide, so the red 'today' deadline flag lands about 635px right of 'Finish expense report' and floats detached from its row. The winner holds the column to about 635px, putting the flag about 200px from the title so it reads as part of the row. Cap the list at a readable max-width of about 640px.  /  The loser stretches each row across a ~1066px-wide column, so the red flag+'today' deadline is pinned at the far right edge (x~1040-1135), about 635px of empty space away from the end of 'Finish expense report'. The eye cannot tie the deadline to its task. The winner caps the list at ~635px (divider ~93-726), so the flag sits ~200px after the title and reads as part of the row. Cap the list content width at ~640px, or bring the flag in next to the title.

composer r6: panel of 3 — desktop 3/3 for ours, phone 1/3 for ours → Things holds — gap: phone: The secondary ink is too heavy. The loser draws the Notes placeholder and all four toolbar glyphs (calendar, tag, checklist, flag) at about #ABABAB, roughly 10 levels darker than the winner's #B5B5B5. They compete with the typed title and outweigh the pale checkbox. The winner keeps the placeholder and toolbar icons lighter, so Buy suitcase reads as the single focal point and the checkbox stays visible (about #C2C2C2 stroke).  /  The loser's bottom tool row (calendar, tag, checklist, flag) sits only ~22px above the card's bottom edge while the checkbox sits ~31px below the top edge, and its glyphs are ~1px larger (24px vs 23px tall) and darker (peak ~#A1A1A1 vs ~#AFAFAF). So the row looks heavier and pushed against the bottom edge. The winner leaves ~24px under 23px glyphs in a lighter tertiary grey, which gives more even top and bottom padding. Fix: add ~2px of padding under the icon row and draw the glyphs 1px smaller in the lighter grey.
composer: phone: lighten notes placeholder + toolbar glyphs, 23px glyphs, more padding under icon row

today r6: pair ready for the critic — Today keeps a compact 312px row measure on desktop (left edge unchanged) so the deadline flag sits ~100px after its title; slimmer Mac moon crescent fitted to Things; This Evening label tracked to Things' width

composer r7: pair ready for the critic — Phone: tool glyphs lightened to tertiary #b4b4b6 and Notes placeholder to #b6b6b8 (matched to Things' ink after the shared pipeline), checkbox ring a shade firmer, 1px more card below the tool row, calendar frame weight matched, and a two-layer shadow fitted to Things' longer bottom drop

today r6: panel of 3 — desktop 1/3 for ours, phone 2/3 for ours → Things holds — gap: desktop: Checklist glyph after 'Buy party decorations': the loser draws its three bullets inconsistently, with two hollow ~5px rings and a solid filled third. Its dashes are uneven ~1px strokes, darker at the start and fading toward the middle, and its note glyph's dog-ear is a filled blob. It reads as noise next to the 17px title. The winner draws three matching bullets with even ~8px x 1.5px bars (~#B8B8B8) and a note glyph with an outlined fold. Fix: make all three bullets identical and the bars uniform in weight.  /  Checklist glyph on the 'Buy party decorations' row (about 19x22px, right of the notes glyph): the loser draws heavy filled bullets about 7px wide next to faint hairline dashes about 10px long, so at 1x it reads as a column of dots, and its notes glyph has a blobby filled dog-ear. The winner uses outlined ring bullets and dashes at the same ~1.5px stroke and ~#A8A8A8 tone, with a thin-line fold on the notes glyph, so both clearly read as checklist and notes. Redraw the loser's glyph with equal stroke weight for bullets and lines.
today: Redraw notes/checklist glyphs: identical ring bullets, even 1.5px bars, outlined note fold

composer r7: panel of 3 — desktop 3/3 for ours, phone 0/3 for ours → Things holds — gap: phone: The text caret in the title field is oversized and rides high: the loser's caret is ~34px tall, starting ~10px above the cap line of 'Buy suitcase' but ending only ~5px below the baseline (~1.8x cap height, top-heavy). The winner draws a ~30px caret centred on the line, ~5px above the cap line and ~5px below the baseline (~1.5x cap height), matching the native iOS insertion point.  /  Near-identical layouts (checkbox, title, Notes and the four toolbar icons all within 1px of each other). The loser's empty checkbox at the left of the title is drawn fainter: about 8% less stroke ink, averaging a light grey around #DADADA. Next to the 25px black title, this weakens the one tappable affordance on the row. The loser also leaves a 16px gap from box to title, where the winner uses 15px. The winner draws the ~20pt rounded box with a slightly firmer grey stroke and keeps it 15px from the title.  /  Text caret collides with the title and sits high: the loser's 2px blue caret at x~199-201 lands on the right stroke of the final 'e' and is ~35px tall, starting ~10px above cap height, so it looks off-centre against the 20px caps. The winner puts the caret 1px clear of the glyph (x~200-202), ~33px tall and centred on the text line. Give the caret a 1px gap after the last glyph and trim it to ~33px, centred on the cap/x-height band. Checkbox, icon row (~#ADADAD, 24px glyphs, 23px bottom inset) and Notes placeholder match to within 1px.
composer: phone caret: trim to ~30-33px centred on line, 1px gap after glyph; firmer checkbox stroke, 15px box-title gap
